# `Q-11-7` — Unrecognized Lua filter handler name

> A Lua filter defines a handler whose name is not an element type
> Quarto knows about, so it will never run.

## What this means

Quarto dispatches filter handlers **by name**: a function called `Str`
runs on every `Str` element, `Para` on every paragraph, and so on. A
handler whose name does not match any element type is never looked up,
so it sits in the filter doing nothing.

Nothing else goes wrong — the document renders, the other handlers run,
and the exit code is zero. That silence is exactly what this warning
exists to break:

```
Q-11-7: Lua filter 'my-filter.lua' defines a handler 'Strs', which is not an
element type Quarto knows about, so it will never run. Did you mean 'Str'?
```

## Why this happens

- **A typo or a plural.** `Strs` for `Str`, `Paragraph` for `Para`,
  `Headers` for `Header`. The suggestion in the message is the closest
  name Quarto recognizes.
- **Wrong case.** Handler names are capitalized exactly as the element
  type is: `CodeBlock`, not `Codeblock` or `codeBlock`.
- **A handler from another tool.** Some Pandoc-adjacent tools and older
  Quarto extensions use names Quarto does not dispatch.
- **A helper function parked on the filter table.** If you return a
  table of handlers, every function in it is treated as a handler. Keep
  helpers in local variables instead:

  ```lua
  local function shout(text)        -- local: not a handler, not warned
    return text:upper()
  end

  return {
    Str = function(elem) return pandoc.Str(shout(elem.text)) end,
  }
  ```

## The handler names Quarto dispatches

Element handlers are named after the element type — `Str`, `Emph`,
`Strong`, `Link`, `Image`, `Code`, `Math`, `Span`, `Para`, `Plain`,
`Header`, `CodeBlock`, `RawBlock`, `BlockQuote`, `BulletList`,
`OrderedList`, `DefinitionList`, `Table`, `Figure`, `Div`, and the
rest.

Alongside them are the handlers that are *not* element types:

| Handler               | Runs on                                   |
| --------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `Pandoc` (or `Doc`)   | the whole document                        |
| `Meta`                | the document metadata                     |
| `Inline` / `Block`    | every inline / every block, whatever its type |
| `Inlines` / `Blocks`  | each *list* of inlines / blocks            |

`traverse` is a setting rather than a handler — it takes the string
`"topdown"`, not a function — so it is never warned about.

## How to fix

Correct the name to the one in the message's suggestion, or remove the
handler if it is dead code. If you believe the name *should* be
supported — it works in Pandoc, or in Quarto 1 — that is worth
reporting: this warning is deliberately noisy about names Quarto does
not know, precisely so that a genuine gap surfaces instead of failing
silently.
